claims.natural_statement: Under all stated exact degree-one compatible symplectic-chart hypotheses of sew:chain, the old report Sections 2-7 supply an analytic prose construction of the uniform positive-radius period-one symplectic immersion and corrected shear charts, with the stated coordinate approximation scope.

For the same hypotheses, N=8*(A+2), K=1024*N**6, c0=64, d=min(1/4,h/(32*c0),r/(32*c0)) and 0<=e<d**7/(1024*K) suffice for b=r/4; the construction also has the passive dependence asserted by RV042_PASSIVE.

For any complex manifold T, jointly holomorphic given chart, shear and lifted-transition data with the same uniform active hypotheses yield a jointly holomorphic period-one map C x Delta_(r/4) x T -> M; symplecticity and immersion are relative to the active (w,p) slices only.

The documented omitted-shear-term and constant-transverse-drift attacks do not refute sew:chain: correct Hamiltonian conjugation cancels the alleged first-order term, and nonzero constant drift has nonzero Liouville period. Bounded period corrections cannot absorb a nonzero constant period over a bi-infinite chain.

The old sewing proof does not discharge the separate K3 geometric supply, continuing-center-buffer, two-family property-L, polydisc, trace-gluing, L-to-CAP and period-transfer obligations. External genus-one and period/dynamics results are scoped source dependencies, not black boxes in the sewing construction.
At least one of the documented shear-omission, nonzero constant transverse-drift, or uniformly bounded flux-repair routes gives an admissible counterexample to the exact annular-chain theorem.
The correct shear-conjugated Hamiltonian correction leaves the alleged first-order a_prime*G_w obstruction used by the old attack.
The constant transverse drift (w,p)->(w,p+c), c nonzero, satisfies the zero Liouville period hypothesis of the exact theorem.
A nonzero constant transition period D can be canceled along all j in Z by uniformly bounded coordinate-change periods c_j satisfying c_(j+1)-c_j=D.

routes.retired_because: The inverse shear differential supplies the a_prime*G_w horizontal term; the Hamiltonian splitting cancels it, so the alleged first-order residual is absent.
The Liouville period of (w,p+c) is c, nonzero for c nonzero; the proposed family violates the exactness hypothesis.

The necessary recurrence c_(j+1)-c_j=D gives c_j=c_0+j*D and is incompatible with uniform boundedness for nonzero constant D; this nonexact route does not refute conditional moving-center recentering.
